title: How Does a Barcode Actually Work?
sources: GS1 / UPC-A basics (GS1 US, barcode references): a UPC-A barcode encodes 12 digits; each digit is drawn as 2 bars and 2 spaces of different widths (7 modules); the 12th digit is a check digit computed from the other 11 so the scanner can catch a misread; the check digit lets the scanner reject most misreads

How scanners read barcodes (Lightspeed 'How do barcodes work'; scanner patents): a red laser/LED light sweeps the code; white spaces reflect light, black bars absorb it; a sensor turns the reflected pattern into on/off signals that decode to the number
The barcode holds only the product number (GTIN), not the price; the store's point-of-sale system looks the number up in its own database to get the name and price (GS1; Lightspeed)

Smithsonian Magazine 'The history of the bar code' and Drexel University obituary of N. Joseph Woodland (2012): Woodland got the idea on a Miami beach in 1948-49 by drawing Morse code dots and dashes in the sand and pulling them downward into thin and thick lines

HISTORY.com 'This day in history, June 26, 1974' and GS1 'Marsh holds place of honor in history of GS1 barcode': the first UPC scan in a store was a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum at Marsh Supermarket in Troy, Ohio, on June 26, 1974

lines.text: Every time a cashier beeps your snacks,
a few black stripes tell the computer what you bought.
lines.caps: A FEW BLACK *STRIPES | TELL THE *COMPUTER | WHAT YOU *BOUGHT

lines.text: So how do lines become a product?
The scanner sweeps a red light across the code.
lines.caps: THE *SCANNER SWEEPS | A *RED LIGHT | ACROSS THE *CODE

lines.text: White gaps bounce it back, black bars soak it up,
lines.caps: WHITE GAPS *BOUNCE | IT *BACK | *BLACK BARS | SOAK IT *UP

lines.text: so the sensor reads on, off, on, off.
and the last one checks for a bad scan.
lines.caps: AND THE *LAST ONE | *CHECKS FOR | A *BAD SCAN

lines.text: Surprise: the barcode doesn't hold the price.
It's just a number the store looks up.
lines.caps: IT'S JUST A *NUMBER | THE STORE *LOOKS UP

lines.text: The idea began as Morse code drawn in beach sand,
lines.caps: THE *IDEA BEGAN | AS *MORSE CODE | DRAWN IN BEACH *SAND

lines.text: And the first thing ever scanned, in nineteen seventy four?
